first_impression: A civic reading court has an overhead wooden louver canopy and a large crafted handwheel mechanism. The keeper is prominent, with two readers behind. Face/hair guidance is clear.

gates.evidence: Both hands belong to the keeper and grip distinct upper/lower portions of the same handwheel rim.
The small toothed piece and large gear overlap in depth without a clear tooth-to-tooth mesh; the handwheel spindle route to a distinct pinion is not readable.
Upper canopy pivots and rods are visible, but no single unbroken crank–rod–tie-bar path connects them to the lower gear.
Broad tilted slats sit above the court and shade bands/boundaries cross the receiving table. This supports the depicted arrangement, not measured control of sunlight.
The neighboring reader shields their eyes, but the book reader already rests hands on a book in mixed light; moving the open book into a clearly new shade boundary is not depicted.
Large readable face, dark bob and separated fringe visibly follow the portrait; no identity claim.
